newsitem.title: USA: Crown Butte likes $65 mln offer for New World mine.
newsitem.headline: Crown Butte likes $65 mln offer for New World mine.

text.p: Crown Butte said it liked the White House's offer of $65 million to stop the company's mine near Yellowstone National Park, but could accept it only if Congress cleared the deal and the company could give up the land, U.S. officials said Friday.
The company said the proposal was "conceptually suitable, if deliverable" in an April 10 letter to the Clinton administration and Montana officials.

The Clinton administration last month offered to pay the company $65 million, fulfilling a campaign pledge to trade assets with the company to block the mine from being developed. The company Thursday reserved the right to withdraw from the agreement to trade the New World Mine property for a federal asset by August 12.

"While Crown Butte has determined not to exercise its 'First Option' to withdraw, it has also determined not to presently give notice that the proposed asset is 'acceptable' and retain its 'Second Option' to withdraw on 12 August 1997," the company's letter said.
Two obstacles to the deal remain -- Congress and Margaret Reeb, the owner of the property on which the gold, silver and copper mine was meant to be.
The main stumbling block for the company is the reluctance of Reeb to allow mining to be permanently barred on her land.
"Crown Butte still has property belonging to Margaret Reeb, which they are responsible for delivering," an Interior Department official said.

While lawmakers in both parties want the company out in order to protect the area from mining pollution, several questioned the buyout and the plan for offsetting it by temporarily trimming the Conservation Reserve Program, which pays farmers not to plant on fragile land.

Farm state lawmakers are bitterly opposed to the proposed offset, despite the administration's insistence it is not planning to cut back the farm program, but just delaying a portion of the payments to farmers.
The Clinton administration has not come up with any other proposal for balancing the $65 million payment in the budget, the Interior Department official said.
Crown Butte chairman Karl Elers, the only company official authorized to comment, was unavailable to talk about the agreement.
